title: Three perfect days in Miami: museums, Coral Gables and Wynwood
dek: Picasso, Klee and Matisse from Berlin at PAMM, a swim in a 1920s coral-rock pool, salsa on Calle Ocho, a seafood festival in Wynwood and NASCAR's title weekend down in Homestead.

hero.caption: The Venetian Pool in Coral Gables, carved from an old coral-rock quarry in the 1920s and still fed with spring water.

intro:
The first weekend of November is when Miami turns back toward the outdoors. The clocks went back on November 1, so the sun now sets at about 5:40 p.m., and the days are made for long lunches and late dinners. The art season is building toward December, and this weekend there is plenty to see before the crowds arrive.

At the Pérez Art Museum Miami, **Picasso–Klee–Matisse: Masterpieces from the Museum Berggruen** opened on October 29: about 100 works from the Berlin collection that the dealer Heinz Berggruen built over four decades, which the museum calls the largest showing of the collection on the East Coast. A new video installation by Zoë Buckman opens there on Thursday, November 5.

It is also a big sports weekend. NASCAR crowns its champions at Homestead-Miami Speedway from Friday to Sunday, the Dolphins play the Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m., and Inter Miami plays Charlotte FC on Saturday at its new Nu Stadium. Expect heavy traffic toward Miami Gardens and Homestead on Sunday.

This plan keeps you clear of the traffic. Friday stays downtown, on the free Metromover, with two museums on the bay and the weekly night market at Miami Worldcenter. Saturday is Coral Gables, from Cuban pastries to the Venetian Pool and the rainforest paths at Fairchild, then salsa in Little Havana. Sunday is Wynwood and Allapattah: murals, the South Florida Seafood Festival, the Rubell Museum, and dinner at Boia De in Little River.

days.title: Friday: downtown and Museum Park
days.intro: A day on the free Metromover, with two museums on Biscayne Bay, a free night market and a Colombian tasting menu on the Miami River.

stops.name: Metromover
stops.text: Start with a ride on the Metromover, the free elevated people mover that loops above downtown and Brickell. From its cars you see the city the way it was built: the river, the towers of Brickell and the bay, a few floors up and with air conditioning. Ride the Omni Loop north to the Museum Park station, which leaves you a short walk from the museums. Trains run from 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day, and there is no fare and no card to buy. Some Brickell Loop stations have had temporary closures this fall, so check rider alerts before you go.

stops.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
stops.text: Come at opening for *Picasso–Klee–Matisse: Masterpieces from the Museum Berggruen*, about 100 works by Picasso, Klee, Matisse, Giacometti, Cézanne and Braque, arranged by still lifes, interiors, portraits and landscapes, alongside Latin American modern works from the museum's own collection by Diego Rivera, Wifredo Lam and Joaquín Torres-García. Leave time for *Basquiat: Figures, Signs, Symbols* and the new Zoë Buckman installation. The museum is open 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Friday to Sunday and closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Book tickets online.

stops.name: Verde
stops.text: The museum's waterfront restaurant and bar has a terrace over Biscayne Bay, the right place to talk over what you have just seen. Order the King Pleasure tiradito of mahi-mahi, empanadas and the grilled fish tacos, or a margherita pizza if you are sharing. Lunch is served from 11 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on Fridays; book a table on OpenTable.

stops.name: Frost Science
stops.text: Next door to PAMM, the Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science has an aquarium, a planetarium and *The Science Behind Pixar*, included with admission. It is the right place for the hottest part of the afternoon or a passing shower, and it works for adults as well as children. The museum is open 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., so arrive by 3 p.m. to see it without rushing, and book tickets online.
stops.wiki: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science

stops.name: Night Market at Miami Worldcenter
stops.text: Every Friday from 5 to 9 p.m., the Paseo at Miami Worldcenter fills with local makers, small food and specialty vendors and live music, next to the historic Pan Am globe. It is free, with no ticket, and it runs rain or shine. Walk over from Museum Park as the light goes, buy a snack and something handmade, and see the newest part of downtown at its liveliest. Vendors change from week to week.

stops.name: Elcielo Miami
stops.text: Juan Manuel Barrientos's restaurant holds a Michelin star for modern Colombian cooking, served as an 18-course Experience Menu that mixes food with small rituals at the table. On Fridays it is $289 a person, and a 20 percent service charge is added. For a lighter evening, the three-course Miami Spice dinner at $65 runs through November 15. Vegetarian and allergy changes are possible if you ask when you book. Dinner starts at 6 p.m.; reserve on OpenTable.

days.title: Saturday: Coral Gables and Calle Ocho
days.intro: Pastelitos and a swim in a 1920s pool, an afternoon under palms and orchids, then dinner on Alhambra Circle and salsa in Little Havana.

stops.name: Tinta y Cafe
stops.text: A Michelin Bib Gourmand for a Cuban cafe: start with a café con leche and pastelitos of beef and guava, then order croquetas, the pavo real of turkey and cream cheese, or the Patria, a Cubano-style sandwich of pork, ham, mustard and pickles that the Michelin inspectors call their favorite. It opens at 8 a.m. on weekends and closes at 4 p.m., so come early and take a second coffee for the walk.

stops.name: Venetian Pool
stops.text: Coral Gables turned a coral-rock quarry into a public pool in the 1920s, with Venetian-style loggias, a stone bridge, grottoes and waterfalls, and it is still filled with spring water. Arrive when it opens at 10 a.m. on Saturday: tickets stop selling once the pool reaches capacity. Admission is $23 for adults and $18 for children aged 3 to 12, and the pool closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekends. Book tickets on the city's site and bring a towel.

stops.name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
stops.text: A 15-minute drive south, Fairchild is 83 acres of palms, rainforest, orchids and lakes. Have lunch first at the Glasshouse Café, which serves until 4 p.m., then take the free tram tour, which runs on a first-come basis, and walk the rest. The garden is open daily from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; parking is free, and arriving by bike or transit takes $5 off an adult ticket. Veterans and active military get in free year-round.

stops.name: Zitz Sum
stops.text: A Michelin Bib Gourmand on Alhambra Circle that cooks Asian food with Miami ideas: Hokkaido scallop crudo acevichado, wonton in brodo with chicken dumplings, potato agnolotti with chili crunch butter and Koshihikari rice with gruyère and a soft egg. Regulars order the bing bread. The seven-course tasting menu is $100 a person, and à la carte works just as well. It serves dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday from 6 p.m.; book on OpenTable.

stops.name: Ball & Chain
stops.text: Ten minutes up the road on Calle Ocho, Ball & Chain's Saturday night, La Pachanga, runs from 8 p.m. to 3 a.m. with live music from 10 p.m., with the singer Lucy Grau and DJs playing salsa, timba and Latin funk. There is no cover, but it is 21 and over, so bring ID. Even if you do not dance, a mojito at the bar and an hour of watching the people who do is a fine way to end a Saturday.

days.title: Sunday: Wynwood, Allapattah and Little River
days.intro: Bread and murals in the morning, a seafood festival for lunch, a private collection in a warehouse and a Michelin-starred Italian dinner.

stops.name: Zak the Baker
stops.text: This Wynwood bakery and cafe is where Miami buys its best bread. Order coffee with a slice of sourdough toast, a bagel or the babka, and buy a loaf for later. Note the schedule: the bakery observes Shabbat, so it is closed every Saturday and on Jewish holidays, which makes Sunday morning the time to go. It opens at 7 a.m., and the line is shortest before 9.

stops.name: Wynwood Walls
stops.text: The outdoor museum of murals that turned a district of warehouses into Miami's best-known art neighborhood, with large works by street artists from around the world, changed over the years. Come when the gates open at 10:30 a.m., before the heat and the crowds. The walls are open every day until 6:30 p.m., and doors close half an hour before. Buy a ticket online, then walk the side streets around NW 2nd Avenue, where the murals are free.

stops.name: South Florida Seafood Festival
stops.text: Lunch is at the 13th South Florida Seafood Festival, back for a second year at Wynwood Marketplace: more than 15 seafood pop-ups, cooking demonstrations, cocktails, live music and DJs, and a market. It runs from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Buy early-bird tickets online: the organizers say prices rise at the door and entry is not guaranteed. Children under 12 go free, and all sales are final.

stops.name: Rubell Museum
stops.text: A short ride west, Don and Mera Rubell show their collection of contemporary art, gathered since 1965, in a converted warehouse in Allapattah. The collection runs to about 7,200 works by more than 1,000 artists, from Basquiat, Warhol, Koons and Cindy Sherman to younger painters. It is open Sundays from 11:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Give it two hours; it is the most rewarding indoor stop of a hot afternoon.

stops.name: Boia De
stops.text: A small Italian restaurant in Little River with a Michelin star, and one of the most sought-after tables in Miami. The Michelin inspectors point to the crispy polenta with marinated eggplant and ricotta salata, the house pastas such as pappardelle with rabbit and rosemary, and veal sweetbreads with beets and jalapeño. It opens at 5:30 p.m. every day. Book on Resy as soon as you can; an early table makes the most of a Sunday that started at a bakery.

stay.name: Faena Hotel Miami Beach
stay.text: Alan Faena's hotel on Collins Avenue, with interiors designed by Baz Luhrmann, its own theater and Francis Mallmann's Los Fuegos for open-fire Argentine cooking. It is on the ocean, with a causeway ride to downtown and Wynwood. For a weekend that is mostly about art, it is the most theatrical place to sleep.

stay.name: The Biltmore Hotel
stay.text: Opened in 1926, with a 315-foot tower and a golf course redesigned by Donald Ross, the Biltmore is the grand hotel of Coral Gables. It puts you a few minutes from Tinta y Cafe, the Venetian Pool and Zitz Sum on Saturday, and away from the beach crowds. Walk through the lobby even if you sleep elsewhere.

stay.name: citizenM Miami Worldcenter
stay.text: A 351-room hotel at 700 NE 2nd Ave, with small, well-designed rooms with big beds, hydromassage showers and an iPad that runs the room. It sits beside the Friday night market and a short walk from PAMM, Frost Science and the Metromover, with Wynwood a short ride north.

events.name: Zoë Buckman: Show Me Your Bruises, Then
events.when: Opens Thu. 11 a.m.; Fri. to Mon. 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.
events.where: Pérez Art Museum Miami, 1103 Biscayne Blvd
events.text: A three-channel video installation in which Buckman, Cush Jumbo and Sienna Miller each recite Buckman's poem about sexual assault, shame and survival, shown with an embroidered antique textile. Included with admission, through May 23, 2027.

events.name: Night Market at Miami Worldcenter
events.text: Free weekly market of local makers, food vendors and live music by the Pan Am globe, rain or shine.

events.name: NASCAR Championship Weekend
events.when: Truck Series Fri. 7:30 p.m.; O'Reilly Series Sat. 5 p.m.; Cup Series Sun. 3 p.m.
events.text: NASCAR's three national series crown their champions at Homestead, with the 400-mile Cup Series title race on Sunday. Day tickets are listed from $51.08 and a three-day pass from $117.47.

events.name: Inter Miami CF vs. Charlotte FC
events.where: Nu Stadium at Miami Freedom Park, near the airport
events.text: A regular-season MLS match (Matchday 34) at the club's new stadium beside Miami International Airport. Allow extra time on the roads around the airport.

events.name: Roda de Samba with Soul Samba
events.where: Miami Beach Bandshell, 7275 Collins Ave, North Beach
events.text: A seven-piece band plays samba Rio-style, around a central table with the audience close in, after a DJ set from Marcello Bentine. Standing tickets from $13.21; free for Miami Beach residents with ID.

events.name: South Florida Seafood Festival
events.text: The festival's 13th year: more than 15 seafood pop-ups, cooking demonstrations, cocktails, live music and a family zone. Buy tickets early online.

events.name: Detroit Lions at Miami Dolphins
events.where: Hard Rock Stadium, 347 Don Shula Dr, Miami Gardens
events.text: The Dolphins host the Lions. The fan zone opens four hours before kickoff, and the roads to Miami Gardens are slow all morning.

know: From Miami International (MIA), take the free MIA Mover to the Miami Intermodal Center and the Metrorail Orange Line downtown: about 25 to 30 minutes to Brickell, at about $2.25 a ride. Ride-hail to downtown or Brickell is roughly $25 to $45, and a car to South Beach takes 25 to 40 minutes. Fort Lauderdale (FLL), the other airport, is farther north.
The Metromover is free and runs from 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, linking Brickell, downtown and Museum Park. Metrorail and Metrobus cost about $2.25 a ride; an EASY Card handles transfers.

Sunday is the busiest day on the roads: the Dolphins kick off at 1 p.m. in Miami Gardens and the NASCAR Cup Series title race starts at 3 p.m. in Homestead. Saturday's 4 p.m. Inter Miami match is next to the airport. Leave extra time for any airport run on Saturday afternoon or Sunday.
The clocks went back on Sunday, November 1, and the sun now sets around 5:40 p.m. Plan pools and gardens for the morning and early afternoon.
Many restaurants add a service charge to the bill (Elcielo adds 20 percent), so check before you tip. Where none is added, 18 to 20 percent is usual.

Opening days matter this weekend: PAMM is closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, the Venetian Pool is closed Mondays, Zak the Baker is closed on Saturdays, and Zitz Sum is closed Sundays and Mondays. Friday's plan is mostly indoors if it rains.
Veterans Day is Wednesday, November 11. Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden admits veterans and active military free all year.
